brief: Do not create any YouTube posts (no YT community posts or carousels). Only one X thread.
brief_reading: Read as: 0 yt_posts and 0 carousel slides (the default is 2 posts with 4 to 6 slides each), and exactly 1 X thread (the default is 2). With no YT post to build from, the one thread is written straight from the transcript. Every other format stays at its default: 4 multi-line X tweets, 2 one-liners, IG companions for the 2 Kaspa tweets, 2 YT polls (yt_text_polls) and X polls for the eligible ones (kaspa, tao). The 2 YT polls are kept because the brief's own parenthetical scopes 'YouTube posts' to community posts and carousels, and the two earlier batches briefed with the same words (was-i-right and best-time) kept their YT polls. If Mike meant no YouTube community content of any kind, delete the two yt_text_polls entries; no image depends on them. Thread topic: the thread follows the stream's main argument (the Nvidia day, the stack of bad news, the midterm lows) and not Kaspa, because Kaspa took around two minutes of this stream (the poll result and the god candle), which carries two tweets, two IG posts and a poll but not a 5 to 8 tweet thread without padding from outside the transcript.

fact_check.claim: 'Jensen Huang reinstated at Nvidia... we had a small pump, but it got eaten up. The Nasdaq 100 closed red, SPX closed green but hardly even did anything' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: CORRECTED. The reinstatement is verified: Nvidia's board restored Jensen Huang as president, CEO and director on Monday November 23 2026, effective immediately (Nvidia press release; CNBC, CNN, NBC, Al Jazeera). The stock market read is wrong on a close to close basis: $NVDA closed up 31% (31.48% to $165.05 per The Motley Fool, after +28% in premarket), the S&P 500 closed at 7,237.17 (+4.73%), the Nasdaq Composite at 24,089.56 (+6.51%) and the Dow +3.01%; CNBC says the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite both had their best day since April 2025. The gains held into the close; Mike was most likely reading the colour of the daily candle bodies after a large gap up at the open. Copy never says stocks closed red or flat. Copy: '$NVDA closed up 31%', 'the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq both had their best day since April 2025', 'stocks had their best day since April 2025'. The Nasdaq-100 close is reported two ways (+6.2% and around +7%) and is NOT printed.
fact_check.source: investor.nvidia.com press release 'NVIDIA Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO and Board Director'; cnbc.com/2026/11/23/nvidia-jensen-huang-ceo.html; cnbc.com/2026/11/22/stock-market-today-live-updates.html (closing levels, fetched 2026-11-24 UTC); fool.com Stock Market Today, Nov. 23 (search result); cnn.com/2026/11/23/business/live-news/jensen-huang-reinstated-as-ceo-of-nvidia

fact_check.claim: 'throughout history, not just with Bitcoin... a lot of times there's a bottom that happens right after the midterm... a year later stocks are up significantly... after Bitcoin, a year later Bitcoin is like double the price' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified and made specific. Bitcoin (Coinbase daily, my calc): the 2018 midterms were November 6 2018 and the bear market low was $3,129 on December 15 2018, 39 days later; one year on (December 15 2019) it closed at $7,111, 2.27x. The 2022 low was $15,460 on November 21 2022, 13 days after the midterms; one year on (November 21 2023) it closed at $35,752, 2.31x. Stocks: the S&P 500 has had no negative one-year return after any midterm election since 1950 (Capital Group; a second tally measured from the last close before Election Day finds the same for every midterm from 1946 to 2022). Copy: '2018: Bitcoin bottomed on December 15, 39 days after the midterms', '2022: it bottomed 13 days after them', 'One year after each of those lows, $BTC had more than doubled', 'The S&P 500 has been higher one year after every single midterm election since 1950'. The line that stocks did this decades before Bitcoin existed follows from the 1950 start date. Nothing in copy says the same must happen this time.
fact_check.source: api.exchange.coinbase.com products/BTC-USD/candles (December 2018, December 2019, November 2022, November 2023); capitalgroup.com/advisor/insights/articles/midterm-elections-markets-5-charts.html; davemanuel.com/2026/10/21/stocks-after-midterm-elections/ (search results, 2026-11-24 UTC)

fact_check.claim: 'AI cracks the Riemann hypothesis in 35 days with a massive proof... 17 million lines of code... this dude was saying it would take humans plus AI until the year 2050, and then 35 days later it gets solved' (transcript, reading a trending headline and a video clip)
fact_check.verdict: CORRECTED and narrowed. Verified: on Friday November 20 2026 Levent Alpoge, a mathematician on Anthropic's technical staff, posted a four-page note saying 'I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis'; the argument is released as around 17 million lines of Lean code; the problem was posed by Bernhard Riemann in 1859 (167 years). His own timeline runs from October 6 to November 16 2026, 41 days, described as around six weeks; '35 days' is the wording of an X trending headline and is NOT printed. Status: outside mathematicians are still working through it (Kevin Buzzard: 'we don't even know why the theorem is true'; some coverage says the Lean and Mathlib communities confirmed that the code checks; no human-readable proof is published; a separate all-human proof was announced the same day and is not mentioned). The '2050' speaker in the clip could not be identified and is not referenced or called out; the general form is sourced to Abhishek Saha (Queen Mary University of London), who said the belief was that a proof would need new theories developed over the next few decades. Copy: 'sat unsolved for 167 years', 'On November 20, a mathematician at Anthropic said he and Claude found a proof in around six weeks', 'around 17 million lines of code, and mathematicians are still working through it', 'A lot of them thought a proof was decades away'. '100 years of discoveries in under five' is Mike's forecast and is written as 'I think'.
fact_check.source: aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/21/riemann-hypothesis-has-the-worlds-most-famous-maths-problem-been-cracked (fetched 2026-11-24 UTC); officechai.com/ai/riemann-hypothesis-in-41-days-levent-alpoges-timeline-shows-how-fast-claude-helped-crack-the-167-year-old-problem/ (fetched); therundown.ai/news/claude-riemann-hypothesis-proof; nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03812-7 and science.org (search results); x.com/i/trending/2124000775961784415 (the '35 days' headline)

tweets.text:
Bitcoin's last bear market bottom: November 21, 2022, after a 28% drop in 15 days. Right after the midterms.

This year's low so far: November 21, 2026, after a 28% drop in 15 days. Right after the midterms.

Here's what I make of it:
tweets.hook: Bitcoin's last bear market bottom: November 21, 2022, after a 28% drop in 15 days. Right after the midterms.

tweets.text:
I think the matching date is a coincidence. The midterms aren't.

2018: Bitcoin bottomed on December 15, 39 days after the midterms.
2022: it bottomed 13 days after them.

One year after each of those lows, $BTC had more than doubled.

And it isn't just Bitcoin.

The S&P 500 has been higher one year after every single midterm election since 1950.

The four-year cycle zombies will call it the halving. Stocks were doing this decades before Bitcoin existed.

So why am I still open to a lower low?

The bad news keeps stacking. The biggest heist in crypto history at Binance on October 29. The midterms. Nvidia losing its CEO for more than a week.

None of those is a black swan by itself. Together they hit like one.

Then on November 23 Nvidia brought Jensen Huang back. $NVDA closed up 31% and stocks had their best day since April 2025.

Bitcoin jumped to $64,500 that morning and gave all of it back by the afternoon.

Good news isn't sticking to crypto yet.

The single biggest thing I'm watching is the Strait of Hormuz.

If that gets resolved, the market starts pricing in that things get better within six months. We go up fast, then retrace to a higher low.

Until then, we can chop sideways down here for a while.

So I don't bet on a date. A new bottom could come next week or two months from now. Nobody knows.

What I know is how the year after the midterms has gone. If we go lower first, that's more deals, and I'm buying assets down here either way.

If this changed how you look at this drop...

Follow me for Bitcoin, Kaspa and macro takes that ignore the four-year cycle echo chamber.

🧠 + 😎
